root_cause_label: Heuristic-Based Pattern Matching Instead Of ELF Parsing
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent adopted a heuristic raw-byte scan for address-value pairs instead of parsing the ELF section headers to identify memory-mapped regions, producing an incorrect and unreliable set of 216 entries.
t_err_evidence: In step 7 the agent decides to scan the entire binary byte-by-byte treating every consecutive non-zero 4+4 byte sequence as an address-value pair, explicitly abandoning any ELF structure-aware approach and writing the first heuristic extract.js.
t_commit_evidence: In step 10 the agent settles on 216 entries from its 'sequence of 3 consecutive pairs' heuristic, treats the count as 'reasonable', and skips ahead in the loop — committing to this output without reconsidering ELF-based parsing.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed that address-value pairs stored in the binary can be reliably identified by looking for consecutive non-zero 8-byte sequences in the raw file. This is false: memory mappings in an ELF binary are defined by the section and program headers (e.g. .text, .data, .rodata), not by arbitrary positional patterns in the raw byte stream.
forewarning_evidence: In step 8 the agent explicitly notes 'I'm concerned that many of these might be false positives since we're scanning every possible 8-byte sequence', indicating awareness that the approach is unreliable — yet it proceeds to refine the same heuristic rather than switch to ELF parsing.
